segments.text: Have you ever read a passage in English class that only made sense after a few reads?
Try this sentence.
The horse raced past the barn fell.
On the first read, it doesn't make sense.
It feels like someone forgot a word.
You reach fell, and the sentence just seems to stop short.
So you read it again.
Wait, did a barn fall, or did the horse raced past the barn afterward?
You test each possibility against the words to see if fell goes with the barn or with
the horse.
Finally, the meaning clicks.
Someone raced a horse past a barn, then the horse fell.
Raced describes a horse, and fell is what the horse did.
Working the sentence out depends entirely on these repeated passes.
Each read updates the meaning until it clicks.
AI does something similar.
It builds meaning through repeated updates.
AI doesn't read your message the way you do.
It processes your text through a series of layers.
Within each layer, steps called attention and transformation work together to update
the numbers, helping the system work out what your words mean together.
The whole stack of layers is called a neural network.
Numbers go in on one side, and final numbers come out the other.
In between stands a long line of layers, one after another, each containing attention
and transformation.
Each row of data passing through contains many numbers, but we are going to focus
on just two to track the change.
We start with a pair at point four two and negative one point one five.
As they pass through the layers, the values shift at every single step, finishing at
point one nine and negative one point one two.
The numbers that come out are not the numbers that went in.
Attention and transformation update the numbers at each layer.
Now let's follow a single word, it, to see how its numbers change in a real sentence.
The cat sat on the mat during the May rainstorm because it was tired.
At the start, the word it could refer to different things.
The starting numbers point one two and negative point three four don't tell us
which one.
By layer one, the numbers update, beginning to capture a connection between it
and cat.
Moving into layer two, the numbers update again.
Now they carry even more specific information about that connection.
This process repeats.
It doesn't stop at layer two.
The numbers continue passing through more layers, each building directly on the
previous layer's numbers.
By the result stage, the two numbers finish at point four one and point zero
six.
AI works out that it refers to cat.
While AI companies don't always share exactly how many layers their models use,
published designs show architectures built with dozens and sometimes more than
a hundred layers.
The horse sentence took a few reads to untangle.
Sarcasm, story twists, and complicated reasoning can take even more work.
AI's layers give it more steps to work through those relationships and build
meaning.
If more layers give the system better reasoning, why not just keep adding them
infinitely?
Because adding layers demands massive amounts of computing power and time.
The extra benefit has to be worth the cost.
Meaning builds up, layer by layer.
Attention and transformation, dozens of times.
